description: Counter that steps a voltage up or down on triggers and wraps round at the top, for stepping through an Array like a sequencer

inputs.text: A rising edge sets the counter back to its first step; it reads high above 2V
A rising edge moves the counter up by the step size, wrapping round to the first step after the last; it reads high above 2V
A rising edge moves the counter down by the step size, wrapping round to the last step after the first; it reads high above 2V
Sets how many steps the counter moves at each trigger, rounded towards zero; 10V is the whole count of steps, or one step per volt when the scale mode is changed, and a negative voltage reverses it

outputs.text: Carries the counter as a voltage: the steps spread evenly from 0V up to 10V, or one volt per step when the output mode is changed

notes: the number under MAX is how many steps the counter runs before it wraps; click it and type a new one, up to 999
the counter moves only on triggers, so nothing changes until INC or DEC is patched
with nothing patched into SCL the step size is 1, and patching a cable holding 0V there sets the step size to zero and stops the counter moving
a polyphonic cable in INC, DEC or RST gives one counter per channel, and a monophonic cable in any of them acts on every counter at once
a trigger at INC and one at DEC in the same sample leave the counter where it is
menu: Scale mode: 10V = max, 1V per step — chooses how SCL is read, either the whole count of steps across 10V or one step per volt
Output mode: max = 10V, 1V per step — chooses what the OUT jack carries, either the steps spread evenly from 0V up to 10V or one volt per step counting from 0V
Offset output by half step — raises the output by half a step, so each step lands in the middle of its share of the range rather than at the bottom

inputs.0:
high above 2V · stepped · polyphonic

a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.1:
high above 2V · stepped · polyphonic

a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.2:
high above 2V · stepped · polyphonic

a negative voltage does nothing here.
